chapter: Road bands: Hucklebuck Williams and Tiny Bradshaw
title: Stage show routines and Curtis Porter's back-beat story
summary: The band turns to showmanship at the Howard Theatre, and Curtis Porter flees a wrong-way back beat at the Glass Bar in St. Louis.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: Shit, you know. And I got tired of that shit but then the band started going--getting to be a tighter band, you know. 'Cause we started playing in the theatres--the Howard, you know, the Howard Theatres and would--opposite other bands.

And those guys used to put on--the saxophone players used to jump on other guys back and they'd be doing all those hootin, hootin stuff, you know. One note things. And the people just go crazy. And so our band, we would come

out there and with our little--with the arrangements and stuff and the people say CLAP, CLAP, you know. You know, so Paul said Close up the books. We don't want no more reading no music--music, man. You going to walk the floor"
Yeah. We had a boy in the band. He used to be--playing, playing Charlie Mingus band-- Shafi (Hadi). And his name was Curtis Porter.

And so, I'll tell you a funny story about him, man. We was in St. Louis in a club called the Glass Bar. And so Paul ... say I want you to walk all around, you know. I want you to dance, want you to dance. Boy, Curtis can use that stuff. So, we're in there playing, man. And this guy forgot to turn the sticks around, you know.

And boy this is how back beat. That back beat thing. My, my -- everytime you would hit that thing, boy looked like my head would just like--and we was--it looked like we did that for about forty-five minutes, man. So Curtis was--walked right on out the door. He went on outside. So Curtis, what he did, he went on outside and so he--and after he got on the outside, he stopped playing. He sat out on the stoop out there. And he said uh, uh, Curtis say, he was sitting down there thinking about how
he'd--how he could get out of the band, you know.
